# Docs: hosted sessions wiki page, wiki index link, graph-manager README ## What to build Documentation only, written after every other hosted-sessions task has landed, so it describes the code as it really is. Three changes: 1. A new wiki page `docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md` in the same format as the other feature pages (Summary, Decisions table with columns Decision | Why | Ticket, Known follow-ups, Code references, Related, Last updated), plus sections for the diagrams, the workspace agent API, the `SessionProvisioner` contract, the environment variables, and how to run the control plane against a local agent for testing. 2. A link to it in `docs/wiki/index.md`. 3. The graph-manager README (`apps/graph-manager/README.md`): accounts and sign-up, the `graph-manager users` command, gateway mode, the database (SQLite default, Postgres), blob storage (folder default, S3), sessions and their caps, Docker sessions, UI plugins, and every new variable in the Configuration table; fix the Security and Limitations sections that still say "one user". No source code changes. `packages/graph-execution` must not change. There is no Jira ticket for this work: in the Ticket column write `hosted-sessions spec`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `docs/prd/hosted-sessions.md` (the whole spec, 378 lines) — the decisions (lines 96–149), the four Mermaid diagrams (lines 34–92), config (175–186), identity/auth (188–192), accounts (194–201), gateway user management (203–205), Docker sessions (207–210), store (212–218), `WorkspaceHost` (220–248), agent (250–255), `SessionProvisioner` (257–272), sessions (274–288), run archive (290–295), UI (297–318), non-goals (151–156). - `docs/wiki/features/sandboxes.md` (whole file) and `docs/wiki/features/multi-repo.md` (lines 1–80) — the page format to copy exactly: `# Title`, `## Summary` with bullets ending in `- Spec: …`, `- Tasks: …`, `- User docs: …`; `## Decisions` table `| Decision | Why | Ticket |`; `## Known follow-ups`; `## Code references` (one bullet per file or group: `` `path`: what it holds ``); `## Related`; `## Last updated` with a date. - `docs/wiki/index.md` — one bullet per feature page under `## Features`; add the new one last. - `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — structure: intro (1–12), Quick start (13–70), **Configuration** table (71–95: `| Env var | Flag | Default (outside Docker) | In the image | Meaning |`), First steps (98–110), Sandboxed runs (112–255), The app (257+), Projects, Agents and tools, Reviewers, Keyboard, Local development (325+), Security (375–379), Limitations (381+). The terminal-ui task already rewrote the Workspaces parts (New terminal dialog, Sessions, Settings → Repositories); keep those and add to them. - The implementation, to get names right (read before writing; quote only what is there): - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` — every `GM_*` variable, its default and its exact error messages. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/identity.ts`, `src/server/auth.ts`, `src/server/routes/gateway.ts` — `X-GM-Identity`, claims, `/api/auth/me`, the gateway disable/delete endpoints. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/accounts.ts`, `src/server/routes/accounts.ts`, `src/server/cli/users.ts` — sign-up, set-password links, `graph-manager users add|list|reset|disable`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/` (`db.ts`, `sqlite.ts`, `postgres.ts`, `migrate.ts`, `migrations/`), `src/server/store.ts` — tables and the import of `graph-manager.json`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/blobs.ts`, `src/server/runarchive.ts` — `BlobStore`, `RunArchive`, blob keys. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/types.ts`, `host/local.ts`, `host/remote.ts`, `host/contract.ts` — `WorkspaceHost`, `RepoRef`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agent/server.ts` (and how the `agent` subcommand is wired into the `graph-manager` bin / `main.ts`) — every `/agent/v1/*` route with its method and body, the PTY WebSocket, `GM_AGENT_TOKEN` rules, `/agent/v1/healthz`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts`, `sessions/docker-provisioner.ts`, `sessions/sessions.ts`, `src/server/routes/sessions.ts` — the provisioner interface, `LocalProvisioner`, `DockerProvisioner`, session states, routes and messages; the idle loop and `/api/notices`. - The hosted-run code (grep `acquireRun`, `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS`, `pushBranch`) and agent logins (grep `loginFiles`, `agentKeys`, `LOGIN_KEYS`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` — projects as `repos: RepoRef[]`, project sessions. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/plugins.ts` and the `/api/ui/plugins` route — the plugin `api`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts` — `buildApp` options (`provisioner`, `store`, `runArchive`). ## Patterns to follow **Decision table row (copy the style of `sandboxes.md`):** ```markdown | Decision | Why | Ticket | | --- | --- | --- | | One container per (user, repository). More terminals on the same repository open as more shells in the same container. | A shell costs a few MB; a container costs real money. | hosted-sessions spec | ``` **Code references bullet:** ```markdown - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/types.ts`, `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/local.ts`: `WorkspaceHost`, `RepoRef` and the local implementation. ``` **README config row (keep the five columns; empty cells for no flag / same in the image):** ```markdown | `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` | | unset (no cap) | same | Caps live sessions (open repositories or projects) per user. Above it, opening another answers 409 "You have 3 open repositories. Close all terminals of one to open another." | ``` Plain, short sentences; no marketing words; exact messages in quotes as the code has them. ## Step-by-step tasks ### CREATE `docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md` - **IMPLEMENT** these sections, in this order: 1. `# Hosted sessions: repo sessions, a workspace agent, accounts, gateway sign-in and session limits` 2. `## Summary` — what changed for a self-hoster (built-in accounts with `admin` keeping the old password; SQLite by default; the Workspaces tab replaced by the New terminal dialog and sessions; Settings → Repositories; Docker sessions once there are two accounts) and for the commercial deployment (gateway sign-in, `RemoteWorkspaceHost` + `graph-manager agent`, a `SessionProvisioner`, caps, UI plugins, hosted runs ending in a PR). Then the bullets: `- Spec: \`docs/prd/done/hosted-sessions.md\`` (it moves there in the PR), `- Tasks: \`.agents/tasks/hosted-sessions/\` (15 tasks)`, `- Ticket: none (hosted-sessions spec).`, `- User docs: "Accounts", "Sessions", "Database and blobs", "Gateway mode" and the Configuration table in \`apps/graph-manager/README.md\`.` 3. `## Diagrams` — the four Mermaid diagrams from the spec, copied verbatim in ```` ```mermaid ```` blocks, each with a one-line caption: hosted (one control plane, one container per open repository), open source on one machine, opening a terminal (sequence), session lifecycle (state diagram). If the code's states differ from the spec's diagram, fix the diagram to match the code and say so. 4. `## Decisions` — one row per decision of the spec (lines 98–149), each rewritten in one or two sentences as built (if the implementation differs from the spec, describe what was built and note the difference in Why), Ticket `hosted-sessions spec` on every row. Include at least: container per (user, repository); branch fixed while live; `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` and its 409 message; all caps env vars and off by default; project session counts as one; projects from forge repositories; hosted runs end in a PR (run container, `gm/`, Create PR into the session branch, the "Uncommitted changes in acme/api are not part of the run." warning, `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS` 409 "You have 3 sandboxed runs. Wait for one to finish or stop it."); local sandboxed runs unchanged; engine unchanged; PR failure keeps `gm/`; per-user forge tokens; closing the last terminal ends the session (waits for a live run); ask before closing (Push to branch / Keep open / Discard); same in open source; secret files never committed (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, git-ignored) and message `graph-manager: save session `; idle backup to `gm/backup/` with the notice; `save-failed` with Retry/Discard; agent logins (login files and Settings → Agents keys from `LOGIN_KEYS`, a key wins); default branch `gm/--<4 chars>`; per-container agent token; the five security points; HS256 identity JWT (claims, ≤ 10 min, 30 s skew); login/logout 404 in gateway mode; built-in accounts (`users` table, scrypt, ≥ 10 characters); upgrade to `admin`; `GM_AUTH=password` alias; sign-up open/closed and `graph-manager users`; no admin role; Settings → Account; cookie with user id and per-username rate limit; gateway user rows; gateway disable/delete endpoints; Docker sessions (`GM_SESSION_RUNTIME`, `gm-user-` volume, 503 message); live sessions keep running when `auto` switches; container hygiene; SQLite default / Postgres optional; the tables; import of `graph-manager.json`; blob storage folder / S3 and the missing-SDK error; the run-folder archive key `runs///.tar.gz`; one control-plane process; what is open source vs commercial; `RunArchive` writes; Settings → Repositories; UI plugins; built on `main`, KAN-96 rebased later; Projects tab stays; every hosted run sandboxed; one graph-execution run. 5. `## Environment variables` — a table `| Variable | Values / default | Meaning |` with every variable this work added, read from `config.ts` and the agent: `GM_AUTH` (`users` default, `password` alias, `gateway`), `GM_SIGNUP` (`closed`/`open`), `GM_DATABASE_URL` (`postgres://` / `postgresql://`), `GM_BLOB_URL` (`s3://bucket/prefix`, with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION`, optional `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`), `GM_GATEWAY_SECRET` (≥ 32 characters, required in gateway mode), `GM_GATEWAY_LOGOUT_URL`, `GM_MAX_SESSIONS`, `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS`, `GM_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`, `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` (`auto`/`local`/`docker`), `GM_UI_PLUGINS`, `GM_AGENT_TOKEN` (agent only, ≥ 32 characters), `GM_TEST_DATABASE_URL` (tests only: runs the database contract suite on Postgres). Note which are stripped from terminal and run environments (`GM_GATEWAY_SECRET`, `GM_AGENT_TOKEN`, `GM_PASSWORD`). Add any other variable the implementation added (grep `GM_` in `config.ts` and the diff of this work: `git log --oneline` / `git diff main --stat` if a `main` ref exists). 6. `## The workspace agent API` — how it is started (`graph-manager agent --port

--workspaces

` with `GM_AGENT_TOKEN`), auth (`Authorization: Bearer ` on everything but `GET /agent/v1/healthz` → `{"ok":true}`; anything else 401), and a table `| Method and path | Body | Answer | WorkspaceHost method |` of every route in `src/server/agent/server.ts` including the PTY WebSocket `/agent/v1/pty/:id`. Copy the routes from the code, not from this task. 7. `## The SessionProvisioner contract` — the interface (copy it from `src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts` as a ```ts block), what each method must do (acquire returns a ready `WorkspaceHost` for a new container running `graph-manager agent`, with a random per-container token; release removes it and never reuses it for another user; `acquireRun`/`releaseRun` for run containers; release is called only after the session's login files were saved and after its live run ended), the two implementations here (`LocalProvisioner`: shared `LocalWorkspaceHost`, `release` no-op, `acquireRun` throws; `DockerProvisioner`: `gm-s-` / `gm-r-` containers, volume `gm-user-` at `/workspaces`, `graph-manager agent --port 7700 --workspaces /workspaces`, waits for healthz, not privileged, no Docker socket), how `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` chooses between them, and how a commercial provisioner is passed in (`buildApp(config, { provisioner, store, runArchive })`). Also the `WorkspaceHost` interface (from `host/types.ts`) as a ```ts block, since a provisioner returns one. 8. `## Testing against a local agent` — step-by-step shell commands that work on a checkout: build (`npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager`), start the agent with a 32+ character `GM_AGENT_TOKEN` on a free port and a temp workspaces dir, `curl` healthz and a 401 without the token, and how the test suite does the same (the shared contract suite `hostContractSuite` in `host/contract.ts` run against `LocalWorkspaceHost` and against `RemoteWorkspaceHost` + a spawned agent in `agent.test.ts`; the command `npm test -w graph-manager -- agent contract`). Also how to try gateway mode locally: start with `GM_AUTH=gateway GM_GATEWAY_SECRET=<32+ chars>` and make a header with `signIdentity` (show a short `node --input-type=module -e` snippet importing it from `apps/graph-manager/dist/server/identity.js`, as the code exports it), and Docker sessions with the fake Docker (`scripts/fake-docker.mjs`, TESTING.md "Sandboxes (fake Docker)"). Run each command you write once to check it works; fix the text if not. 9. `## Known follow-ups` — at least: several control-plane processes behind a load balancer (terminals and in-memory session state live in one process today); a GitHub App (or Sign in with GitHub) instead of personal access tokens; per-plan limits from the gateway instead of one env value per cap; row-level security in Postgres (today isolation is `store.forUser` and owner checks in the routes); the Kubernetes provisioner and warm pool (commercial repo); rebasing `feat/automation-api` (KAN-96) onto this work; plus anything the implementing tasks left open — read the review and tester notes at the end of the run's `run.log` if a `.graph-execution/` folder is present, and the TODOs in the new files (`grep -rn "TODO\|follow-up" apps/graph-manager/src/server/{sessions,host,agent,db}`). 10. `## Code references` — one bullet per area with the real paths: identity and auth; accounts and the users CLI; gateway routes; db layer and migrations; store; blobs and run archive; host (types, local, remote, contract); agent; sessions (provisioner, docker provisioner, manager, routes, idle loop, notices); hosted runs; agent logins and Settings → Agents; projects; web (New terminal dialog, sidebar, close dialog, Settings → Repositories / Account / Agents, login/signup/set-password pages, plugins, notices banner). Check every path exists (`ls`). 11. `## Related` — links to `graph-manager.md`, `sandboxes.md`, `multi-repo.md`, `agent-tools.md`, and `../index.md`. 12. `## Last updated` — today's date (`date +%F`). - **VALIDATE**: every path in Code references exists: `grep -o '`apps/[^`]*`' docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md | tr -d '`' | tr ',' '\n' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'test -e "{}" || echo MISSING {}'` prints nothing. ### UPDATE `docs/wiki/index.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: append under `## Features`: `- [Hosted sessions: repo sessions, a workspace agent, accounts, gateway sign-in and session limits](features/hosted-sessions.md)`. - **VALIDATE**: `grep -n hosted-sessions docs/wiki/index.md` ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: - Intro bullets (lines 3–9): add "sign in with your own account (or several people on one server, each with their own data)". - **Configuration** table: one row per new variable, same five columns, values and messages as in `config.ts`: `GM_AUTH`, `GM_SIGNUP`, `GM_DATABASE_URL`, `GM_BLOB_URL` (+ the AWS variables in one row), `GM_GATEWAY_SECRET`, `GM_GATEWAY_LOGOUT_URL`, `GM_MAX_SESSIONS`, `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS`, `GM_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`, `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME`, `GM_UI_PLUGINS`. Update the `GM_PASSWORD` row: it is now the password of the `admin` account (set at every start while it is set) and is not read in gateway mode. Update the `GM_DATA_DIR` row: it holds `graph-manager.db` (SQLite), `blobs/`, the generated password and `bin/`; an old `graph-manager.json` is imported on first start and renamed `graph-manager.json.imported`. - New section **Accounts** (after Configuration or after First steps): sign-in with username and password (`admin` for an upgraded install, with its old password); `GM_SIGNUP=open` shows **Create account**; with the default `closed`, `graph-manager users add ` prints a one-time link valid 7 days, `users list`, `users reset ` (a new link), `users disable ` — give the exact command as the bin wires it (from npm: `graph-execution manager users …` if that is how it is wired; check `src/server/cli/users.ts` and the bin). Settings → Account changes the display name and password (other sign-ins end). No admin role: every user has their own forge tokens, reviewers, sandbox recipe, repository settings, run defaults and agent keys. Settings → Agents: API keys per provider. - New section **Sessions and limits**: extend what the terminal-ui task wrote: caps `GM_MAX_SESSIONS`, `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS`, `GM_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` (off by default) with their messages, the idle backup branch and notice, project sessions (one session for all repositories of a project), and **Docker sessions**: with two or more accounts and `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=auto`, each session runs in its own container with the user's volume `gm-user-`; without Docker opening a session answers the exact 503 message; `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=local` turns it off for people who trust each other. - New section **Database and blobs**: SQLite at `/graph-manager.db` by default (nothing to install); `GM_DATABASE_URL=postgres://…` for Postgres; the stop message `Cannot connect to the database: `; run folders archived as `.tar.gz` under `/blobs/` or in S3 with `GM_BLOB_URL=s3://…` (needs `npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3`, else the exact startup error); the Runs page keeps ended runs read-only. - New section **Gateway mode** (for running behind your own sign-in service): `GM_AUTH=gateway`, the `X-GM-Identity` HS256 token (claims `sub`, `name`, optional `email`, `iat`, `exp`, ≤ 10 minutes), 401 `{"error":"gateway identity required"}`, login/logout 404, `GET /api/auth/me`, `POST /api/gateway/users/:id/disable` and `DELETE /api/gateway/users/:id` with `Authorization: Bearer `, `GM_GATEWAY_LOGOUT_URL`, and a pointer to the wiki page for the agent and provisioner. - **UI plugins**: `GM_UI_PLUGINS` and the `api` (`React`, `registerNav`, `registerRoute`, `registerTopbar`, `registerSettingsSection`), a 5-line example module. - **Security**: replace "Anyone who can log in can run any command there and read the tokens" with the multi-user truth: with one account, terminals run as the server's user; with two or more, sessions run in Docker containers (unless `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=local`) and each user sees only their own data; `GM_GATEWAY_SECRET`, `GM_AGENT_TOKEN` and `GM_PASSWORD` never reach terminals or runs; tokens are in the database (SQLite file mode 600 if the code sets it — check). - **Limitations**: remove "One user per deployment (a single admin password)."; add "One graph-manager process per database: several behind a load balancer is not supported yet." and "Terminals do not survive a restart" stays. - Link the new wiki page from the README where the agent/provisioner is mentioned: `[hosted sessions](../../docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md)`. - **GOTCHA**: do not undo the terminal-ui task's changes (no Workspaces page, New terminal dialog, Settings → Repositories, the keyboard table). Read the current README fully before editing. - **VALIDATE**: `grep -n "One user per deployment\|Workspaces →\|g w" apps/graph-manager/README.md` prints nothing; every `GM_` variable in `config.ts` appears in the README: `for v in $(grep -o 'GM_[A-Z_]*' apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts | sort -u); do grep -q "$v" apps/graph-manager/README.md || echo "missing $v"; done` (internal or test-only variables may be skipped on purpose: list them in your final note). ### UPDATE the root `README.md` (only if needed) - If its "The web app" section (lines 35–43) still says graph-manager has one password or one user, change it to accounts (username and password; optional sign-up). Keep it short. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md` exists with Summary, Diagrams (the four Mermaid diagrams), Decisions table (Decision | Why | Ticket, Ticket = `hosted-sessions spec`), Environment variables, The workspace agent API (every `/agent/v1/*` route from the code), The SessionProvisioner contract (interface + Local and Docker implementations), Testing against a local agent (commands that work), Known follow-ups (including several control-plane processes, GitHub App, per-plan limits, row-level security), Code references (all paths exist), Related, Last updated. - [ ] `docs/wiki/index.md` links to it. - [ ] The graph-manager README documents accounts, sign-up, the users command, gateway mode, the database, blobs, sessions and their caps, Docker sessions and UI plugins, and lists every new `GM_*` variable in the Configuration table; "One user per deployment" is gone. - [ ] No source file changed; `packages/graph-execution` is unchanged. - [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass (nothing in code changed, so this checks nothing broke). ## Validation commands ```bash # Type / lint (docs-only task: these must still pass) npm run typecheck && npm run lint # Tests npm test -w graph-manager -- agent contract # Docs checks test -f docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md && grep -q "features/hosted-sessions.md" docs/wiki/index.md && echo docs-ok grep -c '```mermaid' docs/wiki/features/hosted-sessions.md # 4 or more git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution apps/graph-manager/src # must print nothing ```
